DropLabREAL-WORLD PLAY
The evidenceStreamer's guide

01 / THE PROBLEM

Watching is easy.
Taking part needs a question.

A viewer can watch a science experiment without ever making a prediction. And when a paper helicopter falls in about a second, a casual stopwatch can make a close call look certain.

Chat needs a question before the drop and evidence after it.

02 / Our solution ↓03 / Try what we built ↓04 / See the results ↓
ONE SMALL EXPERIMENT

"Will it stay airborne
for one second?"

No prediction before it fallsNo clear evidence after it lands

02 / HOW WE SOLVE IT

Make a call.
Then let the evidence answer.

DropLab gives a Twitch community one shared question, locks predictions before playback and shows the range the footage supports.

01

Predict before the outcome.

Chat chooses Yes or No. The host locks the round before anyone sees the drop.

02

Review what really happened.

Release and landing windows give a possible flight-time range. A close call can stay unresolved.

03

Choose the next question.

After the result, chat can propose longer blades, a paper clip or another repeat.

04 / RESULTS

What we have verified.

Read the test record ↗
1 real Twitch prediction

Received from the creator's channel and followed through lock, recorded replay and the synchronized result.

0 practice · 0 sample in that check
3 physical recordings

Reviewed release and landing windows. The default rounds demonstrate Yes, Too close to call and No.

Manual timing · same helicopter
27 + 6 checks passed

27 software tests and six browser scenarios covered the round, chat parser, overlay, export and phone layout.

Technical validation · no adoption claim

The result so far is a working prototype with a verified Twitch interaction. We have not measured learning gains or audience engagement, and the overlay check was not a live broadcast.

YOUR ROUND / THE EVIDENCE

A result you can inspect.

The camera moved, so automatic tracking wasn't reliable. We reviewed the release and landing frames instead. The result is a time range, with room for what the footage can't settle.

01

Commit to a prediction.

Viewers type a simple command. The host locks every choice before revealing the drop.

02

Let the real world answer.

Watch a real paper helicopter fall. The three recordings are replayed, never passed off as live footage.

03

Leave room for uncertainty.

If the timing range straddles the prediction line, the round is too close to call. No invented winner.
